content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name] and [product_name] (software), and I'm just starting with automated home lighting. I'm struggling with programming a feature that feels like it should be simple, but I've been unable to get it working. I want my push-buttons to react to a 'double click' within about two seconds. If the button is pressed once, after two seconds Q1 should turn on. If pressed twice quickly, then Q1 should stay off and Q2 should be activated. Does anyone have suggestions for an easy way to implement this? Ideally, I'd like to make a reusable function for this, so any button can turn everything off, or even serve as a panic button if pressed multiple times, like four clicks. Thanks!

Hi, Maybe the attached program will help. It works as follows: single click turns on Q1 after two seconds, double click when Q1 is off turns on Q2, second click when Q1 is already on turns Q1 off and Q2 on, and a third click turns everything off. Regards,
Hi [user_name], Check my answer in the 'Double tap button' discussion and see the updated example in the attachment. Best regards [user_name]
Thank you, [user_name]. It's not exactly what I needed, since I'll need to modify the 'second click and Q1 on' behavior to instead turn everything off, but your input was still very helpful!

Thanks! I found your original example, and it works well (the keyword 'tap' is useful for searching). With your latest version, if I just tap the button once, somehow all three Q outputs activate one after another (which actually works nicely for stair lighting). Is this the intended behavior?
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled '[product_name] [version_no], Request help to design debouncing for multi button circuit.' Best regards [user_name]
